title: QUIC Server-Role Managed TLS Crypto Floor Verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home tests and inspection evidence for the narrow server-role ClientHello to ServerHello crypto floor behind the existing transcript-progress and bridge-driver seam.
expected_result: The server role accepts only the supported ClientHello subset for TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 over secp256r1 or the bounded first-flight x25519 branch, tolerates non-conflicting unknown ClientHello extensions, supported_versions lists that include TLS 1.3, and psk_key_exchange_modes lists that include psk_dhe_ke, preserves staged peer transport parameters from that ClientHello, constructs one local ServerHello, exposes those bytes through the existing Handshake crypto-output seam, publishes explicit Handshake open/protect material and Handshake key availability only after the ClientHello plus ServerHello transcript boundary exists, rejects malformed or unsupported ClientHello progression deterministically, and still leaves server-role commit and wider handshake support unavailable.
procedure: Run the CRT requirement-home tests that cover the supported server-role ClientHello path, compatibility ClientHello extension tolerance, outbound ServerHello exposure, Handshake key-availability publication ordering, malformed framing rejection, unsupported version or cipher-suite rejection, unsupported named-group or key-share rejection, and repeated or conflicting progression rejection.

Run the RFC9001 requirement-home tests that still cover outbound Handshake packet emission, Handshake packet protection, transport-parameter staging, and deterministic rejection of malformed Handshake packet input on the bridge seam.

Inspect the preserved server-local quic-go handshake rerun at `artifacts/interop-runner/20260422-110409619-server-nginx/` and the hosted neqo connectionmigration run `25867235353` together with the captured replays in `tests/Incursa.Quic.Tests/RequirementHomes/CRT/REQ-QUIC-CRT-0112.cs` to confirm the relevant live failures are represented as deterministic local ClientHello fixtures rather than listener startup or report-capture issues.

Inspect the bridge driver, transcript-progress owner, and key-schedule implementation to confirm the slice stays inside the main library seam, keeps runtime or host wiring unchanged, keeps commit unavailable, and does not add native TLS fallback.
scope: This slice verifies only the permanent server-role crypto floor from peer ClientHello through local ServerHello and Handshake packet-protection material availability. It does not prove EncryptedExtensions, certificate flight, server Finished, client-certificate authentication, 0-RTT, 1-RTT, key update, endpoint-host wiring, or interop-runner handshake support.
preconditions: The tests project can access internal library seams through the existing friend assembly relationship.
status_summary: Passed on 2026-05-14; focused requirement-home tests prove the supported server-role ClientHello to ServerHello floor, compatibility tolerance for non-conflicting unknown ClientHello extensions, supported_versions lists that include TLS 1.3, and psk_key_exchange_modes lists that include psk_dhe_ke, Handshake key-publication ordering, deterministic malformed-input rejection, and the intentional rejection of unsupported named-group or key-share input outside the current subset. Earlier preserved server-local quic-go handshake reruns showed the listener reaching the live handshake path; hosted neqo proof evidence reached a real peer ClientHello and failed with TLS alert 50 before migration could begin until the captured neqo ClientHello replay was added as local proof.
